label: input e early in the sequence after specific preceding tokens (c e / [k,a,c] _ e / L=3 echoed first token e)
explanation: Very sparse token detector for input e (99.5% of activation mass is on in_tok=e). It fires only at the start of the sequence: t=1 (20% of mass), t=2 (60%), or t=4 in L=3 sequences, where the fed-back first output e is the input (20% of mass, and this is where the largest activations occur, e.g. e a n <DEL> [e]). It does not fire on e at t=0, t>=3 in the original phase, at the delimiter, or later in the copy phase. Within those positions it depends on the preceding tokens like a lookup table: at t=1 it fires every time the prefix is c e (precision 1.0) and never after other first tokens; at t=2 it fires mainly when the token two back is k, a or c (also y or c as the previous token). Precision is incomplete because the prefix dependence at t=2 is a scattered set of token pairs that this predicate only approximates. Magnitude is largest on the L=3 copy-step case and on k c e / k q e prefixes; the t=1 c e cases are weak (about 0.07 of max).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 37 cues. Raise it: t=2 & in_tok=e (+4.27), in_tok=e (+3.71), t=1 & in_tok=e (+3.04), t=2 & prev_tok=y (+3.03), t=1 & prev_tok=c (+2.78), prev2_tok=k (+2.52). Lower it: in_first=0 (-1.67), prev_tok=w (-1.45), prev_tok=0 (-1.42), L=7 (-0.30).
